chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Tawaf (circumambulation of the Kaaba), for those other than the inhabitants of Makkah, is superior to the Salat (Prayer); and the Salat (Prayer) for the inhabitants of Makkah is superior.

key_terms.الطَّوَافُ: Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: Which is more virtuous: Tawaf or Salat, for residents versus non-residents of Makkah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a comparative ruling between the ritual of Tawaf and the daily Salat, noting that for non-residents of Makkah, performing Tawaf holds greater merit than performing Salat, whereas for the residents of Makkah, the Salat is superior to Tawaf. This distinction highlights the unique status of the Ahl al-Makkah, who are exempt from the obligation of Hajj and thus maintain a continuous spiritual connection through their local prayers, while visitors are rewarded for the specific act of circumambulation. The hadith underscores the flexibility in Islamic jurisprudence regarding the relative virtues of acts of worship based on the worshipper's residency and obligation status.
